title: Warmth gave no clear link to pair-based beetle dominance in four English and Scottish samples in 1993-2015
abstract: We tested whether collection-period warmth had a repeated link to dominance in beetle catches. We used 2,605 selected ten-trap collections in England and Scotland in two periods from 1993 to 2015. The index is the chance that two distinct caught individuals have the same taxon code. Models controlled location by month, year, rain and collection timing. All four adjusted year-cluster intervals included zero. Slopes ranged from -0.0368 to +0.0043 probability units per degree C. Removing the finite-catch term in the usual squared-share index gave no clear common slope change. One larger-catch check gave a negative early Scottish estimate. Selected catches, few sites, coarse weather and unequal capture limit inference. The result does not show no effect and does not test air pollution or causal climate change. Code, exact source hashes, aggregate evidence, checks and a static figure support review and reproduction. External records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Warmth slopes of distinct-pair concentration and of the usual index minus the pair index. All primary adjusted intervals include zero. Year clusters and a four-test adjustment are used.
